thesis: Induction composes declared typed primitives into programs whose reuse and total cost must be independently evaluated.

ideas.statement: Induction composes declared typed primitives into programs whose reuse and total cost must be independently evaluated.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Grouping by identity, selecting a last event and interpreting its type can become a parameterized shared program.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Types and brevity do not establish truth; program equivalence is restricted and held-out evaluation cannot be reused adaptively without consequences.

audit.notes: Source-grounded analysis; proposed mechanisms and limited guarantees preserved.
